name: MyGo
one_liner: Build desktop apps in Go with a web frontend or a native UI; each app ships as one binary of a few megabytes.

text.why: Desktop apps often carry a whole bundled web runtime. MyGo uses the webview already on the OS or draws a native UI on the GPU, aiming for small apps with low memory and CPU use.
text.take: One app can mix web and native windows.
build: Pure Go with no cgo, so you can build for every platform from any machine. Web pages call Go through a TypeScript client generated from your Go code, and there is a native toolkit with layout, widgets and screen-reader support. Windows, menus, tray, notifications, installers, signing and auto-updates are included.

who.role: Go developers who want to ship small desktop apps.

start.text: Create a project with bunx mygo-cli init my-app, as the website shows.

caveat: An early project at version 0.2.6 with about 320 stars; macOS, Linux and Windows are listed.

license.scope_text: Use, change and redistribute, commercially too. Keep the notice.

numbers.star_delta_unit: GitHub stars gained in the window, GH Archive events summed to as_of
numbers.method: Star total = the value last checked on GitHub (stars_checked_at) + increases observed via GH Archive since. The 24h · 7d · 30d gains are GH Archive hourly events summed to the reference time (as_of). No score of ours.

notes: This file was produced by the same build, from the same data, as the tesign.com item page. The text is editorial; the numbers are stored observations.
